title.narrative: National Disaster Risk Management Project (Supplemental Financing)

description.narrative: The proposed project will support the Government of Tajikistan in managing the expected increased severity and frequency of disasters triggered by natural hazards in the country and in reducing the socioeconomic vulnerability of Tajikistan to natural hazards. It will (i) support government efforts to mainstream disaster risk management (DRM) in development planning, and (ii) lay a foundation for establishing a sustainable institutional and financial mechanism that enables Tajikistan to deal effectively with disasters in the long term.

description.narrative: Output/s as listed by the project staff.

Output: Capacity to manage natural hazards and minimize losses strengthened Indicator: Community-based DRM and DRM awareness in educational institutions in high-risk districts and cities implemented, including at least 40% women Achievement: Y Progress/Status: Completed.
The Aga Khan Agency for Habitat (AKAH) conducted a kick-off session regarding the CBDRM program in May 2022. The CBDRM program was conducted within the high-risk districts and villages to achieve the objectives of CBDRM. AKAH implemented the CBDRM program in 63 villages covering 29 high risk districts in all four regions of Tajikistan. The program reached 1,869 community members of whom 1,035 (55%) were women. Women participation ranged from 7% to 73% when disaggregated by individual villages. CESCD has verified the accomplishment of this sub-output and has considered the task as successfully completed. Data Source: QPRs of executing agency, executing agency's PCR Baseline year: 2018 Baseline value: Not applicable Baseline year: 2018 Baseline value: Not applicable Target year: 2021 Target value: Y Actual value: Y

Output: Capacity to manage natural hazards and minimize losses strengthened Indicator: Early warning system established Achievement: Y Progress/Status: Completed.
The Doppler Weather Radar, which was a new installation, was operational in August 2021, and the monitoring and early warning system for Sarez Lake was commissioned in September 2021. In November 2022, ADB granted approval for the procurement of (i) EWS equipment for CESCD and (ii) replacement parts and batteries for existing EWS mobile communications equipment. The Quotation Evaluation Reports (QERs) were approved on 24 January 2023 and the contracts were awarded to AT Communication International LLC (Georgia) in the amounts of $83,982 and $79,170 respectively. The contracts were successfully completed on 4 May 2023. The CESCD EWS communication system was improved by incorporating the additional pieces of equipment. The PIC provided a concept paper regarding the design of a national EWS and a conceptual design of multi-hazard early warning system (MHEWS) on 6 November 2023 for review and acceptance by CESCD. CESCD has reviewed the MHEWS conceptual report and the MHEWS Remote Sensing and Services report and find them to satisfy the requirements of CESCD. Both reports will support CESCD to present and develop a responsive national EWS approach in collaboration with other Line Ministries through the National Platform for Disaster Risk Reduction. CESCD has accepted the Multi-hazard Early Warning System reports. Data Source: QPRs of executing agency, executing agency's PCR Baseline year: 2018 Baseline value: Not applicable Baseline year: 2018 Baseline value: Not applicable Target year: 2022 Target value: Y Actual value: Y

Output: Capacity to manage natural hazards and minimize losses strengthened Indicator: Hazard maps and inventory of assets at risk based on a detailed assessment, national risk profile, multi-hazard vulnerability, and risk assessments that consider social factors such as sex, age, ability, and income and poverty levels prepared Achievement: Y Progress/Status: Completed.
The Multi-hazard risk profiles for the Gorno-Badakhshan Autonomous Oblast (GBAO), Sughd, Regions of Republican Subordination (RRS), and Khatlon regions were prepared by October 2022 and underwent a final review from a climate change and gender perspective and were submitted to CESCD on 26 October 2023 for their review and acceptance. CESCD has reviewed the four profiles and find them to satisfy the requirements of CESCD. The profiles are written in a style that enables CESCD to develop and promote risk reduction programs that are specific to the hazards of each of the four regions. The profiles also link directly to the link to the risk reduction measures presented in the Nine-year Investment plan. CESCD has accepted the four Regional Multi-hazard Risk Profiles. Data Source: QPRs of executing agency, executing agency's PCR Baseline year: 2018 Baseline value: Not applicable Baseline year: 2018 Baseline value: Not applicable Target year: 2020 Target value: Y Actual value: Y

The contract to develop and implement the DMIS was awarded to the Integrated Project Services LLP, based in Kazakhstan, for the sum of $197,000.00, and completed on 28 September 2023. CESCD confirmed to ADB that they have received DMIS Version 1.0 and that the DMIS is operational. The EA has acknowledged and accepted the deliverable. Output: Capacity to manage natural hazards and minimize losses strengthened Indicator: National, regional, district, and sector DRM plans prepared Achievement: Y Progress/Status: Completed.
The National DRM plan was complete, and a stakeholder consultation workshop was held on 10 November 2023. The National DRM plan was finalized and submitted to CESCD on 30 November 2023. The disaster risk management plan will support sector strategies and CESCD's input to the National Platform for Disaster Risk Reduction. CESCD has reviewed the National DRM Plan and find that it satisfies CESCD's request to produce a DRM plan that is strategic and that will support the development of responsive sector strategies by the Line Ministries and CESCD's input to the National Platform for Disaster Risk Reduction. CESCD has accepted the National Disaster Risk Management Plan. Output: DRM mainstreamed in government institutions Indicator: CESCD 5-year business and/or operational plan (2021-2025) with gender-specific actions developed Achievement: Y Progress/Status: Completed.
This output indicator was contingent upon the outputs derived from output indicators 1a, 1d, 1c, and Training plan implemented. The PIC reviewed the pre-existing organizational structures, operational management systems, and the delineation of roles and responsibilities within various departments, divisions, and units of CESCD. Subsequently, CESCD reached a consensus on its DRM Vision, Mission, and a set of Objectives. In June 2021, the PIC presented the final Five-Year Business Operational Plan (2021-2025) for CESCD, which encompassed the identification of research and data requirements, as well as established implementation targets and project outcomes. The deliverable has been completed. Data Source: QPRs of executing agency, executing agency's PCR Baseline year: 2018 Baseline value: Not applicable Baseline year: 2018 Baseline value: Not applicable Target year: 2021 Target value: Y Actual value: Y

Output: DRM mainstreamed in government institutions Indicator: CESCD institutional plan with capacity building for gender-responsive DRM implemented Achievement: Y Progress/Status: Completed.
The EA and Project Implementation Consultant (PIC) established official Technical Working Groups (TWG) within each ministry or agency and cultivated partnership with development partners. The tasks included a comprehensive review of DRM policies, national strategies, and institutional provisioning documents, as well as conducting an in-depth institutional functional survey of seven sectors and eight departments of CESCD. This also entailed the formulation of a vision and mission statement and objectives for CESCD, determining the role of CESCD within the realm of DRM, outlining departmental functions, analyzing the inter-agency linkages for CESCD's business process model, and proposing three options for the reorganizing of CESCD institutionally. The activities under Sub-output 1 were completed by PIC as of December 2021 and the EA has accepted the deliverable.
The CESCD institutional plan, which includes capacity-building initiatives for gender-responsive Disaster Risk Management implemented (DRM). The CESCD has confirmed on 22 July 2024 and provided supporting documents on 24 May 2024. Data Source: QPRs of executing agency, executing agency's PCR Baseline year: 2018 Baseline value: Not applicable Baseline year: 2018 Baseline value: Not applicable Target year: 2020 Target value: Y Actual value: Y

Output: DRM mainstreamed in government institutions Indicator: DRM-integrated sector strategies, with actions that address specific needs of women, children, elderly, and people with disabilities, approved Achievement: Y Progress/Status: Completed.
The PIC, in collaboration with the designated focal points representing the seven sector ministries/agencies, successfully incorporated DRM, Climate Change, gender equality, and social inclusion issues in sectoral strategies of the following entities: the Ministry of Health and Social Protection, the Ministry of Education and Science, the Ministry of Transport, and the State Management Committee for Land Management and Geodesy. In addition, these considerations have been mainstreamed into the draft Mid-term Development Program of the Republic of Tajikistan for 2021 to 2025, and the Adaptation section of the Nationally Determined Contributions (NDC) for Tajikistan. The final deliverable was duly submitted by June 2021 and the EA has officially accepted the deliverable. Data Source: QPRs of executing agency, executing agency's PCR Baseline year: 2018 Baseline value: Not applicable Baseline year: 2018 Baseline value: Not applicable Target year: 2021 Target value: Y Actual value: Y

Output: DRM mainstreamed in government institutions Indicator: Draft legislation providing a single, comprehensive law on DRM prepared Achievement: Y Progress/Status: Substantially achieved.
The PIC finalized the production of Legal Briefs and conducted an extensive Detailed Legal Review of the country's legal framework pertaining to Climate Change and Disaster Risk Management (CCDRM). In response to CESCD's request, the PIC also authored a Comments Paper concerning the Draft Law on Civil Protection, incorporating findings and recommendations based on a comparative analysis against international standards and good practice. The integration of gender equality and social inclusion consideration into national legal instruments and sector-specific laws pertaining to CCDRM was diligently addressed. Furthermore, the PIC was tasked by CESCD to formulate an Options Paper aimed at strengthening the national DRM Law, which also included the development of provisions related to climate change, gender equality and social inclusion, vulnerable groups, and international assistance. The activities were successfully concluded by January 2021 and the deliverable has been accepted by the EA.
The CESCD has confirmed on 22 July 2024 and provided supporting documents on 24 May 2024. Data Source: QPRs of executing agency, executing agency's PCR Baseline year: 2018 Baseline value: Not applicable Baseline year: 2018 Baseline value: Not applicable Target year: 2018 Target value: Y Actual value: Y

Output: Road map for investments and sustainable financing developed Indicator: -year DRM investment plan (2022-2030) prepared by December 2021 Achievement: Y Progress/Status: Completed.
The nine-year investment plan and an options paper on funding opportunities to support the investment plan as a road map for funding, were completed in June 2022. The investment plan is supported by an economic analysis for each of the four regions of Tajikistan. The principal investments with respect to natural hazards risk mitigation are improvements to the regional transportation corridors, earthquake resilient structures, flood protection, and reforestation initiatives. Soft investment in CBDRM and awareness raising are proposed cornerstone investments for natural hazards risk mitigation. The review of the nine-year investment plan was submitted in July 2022 to incorporate suggested methodology, if aligned with methodology stipulated in the TOR and approved during the inception report.
A comprehensive report on funding opportunities to support the investment plan, as a guide for securing financing was finalized. The financing mechanisms included public funding, targeted local public funding, counterpart funding, and the establishment of a Trust Fund. The EA is in the process of engaging with the Ministry of Finance, Sector Ministries/Agencies, higher government authorities, and Development Partners. The objective is to propose an approach that development partner agencies could utilize to allocate funding to Disaster Risk Reduction programs, projects, and activities in Tajikistan.
